column1: # Hammet Palace: pre-rescue secrecy and private fear; post-rescue gratitude, guard security and Shaman's Rod.

column3: A soldier's turban rests\nhere. The cloth has been\ncarefully folded.{end_wait}
A book on trading lies\nopen. Its advice is simple:\nkeep your word, or lose{page_break}your customers.{end_wait}
A book on hospitality.\nSomeone has marked the part\nabout remembering each{page_break}guest's needs.{end_wait}

Dodonpa knows how to get
what he wants. For all we
know, his men are watching{page_break}Kalay. Sending troops could
put Hammet at risk.{end_wait}
The townspeople don't know\nHammet was taken, do they?\nI hope it stays that way{page_break}until we can help him.{end_wait}
Hammet will come home. He\nhas to. Don't you think?{end_now}
Layana speaks calmly to\neveryone. When the hall is\nempty, she barely says a{page_break}word.{end_wait}

Kalay's traders are
supposed to be safe on
these roads. Dodonpa knows{page_break}that, and takes hostages
anyway.{end_wait}
If Hammet never returns,\nwho will lead his caravans?\nWhat happens to Kalay?{end_now}
Hammet, am I doing the\nright thing? Every choice\nseems to put you in danger.{end_wait}

The townspeople ask where
Hammet is. We've told them
he's away on business. I{page_break}don't know how long they'll
believe it.{end_wait}
Everyone here knows\nsomething is wrong. No one\nwants to be the first to{page_break}say it aloud.{end_wait}
I heard Lady Layana crying\nlast night. This morning\nshe thanked me as if{page_break}nothing had happened.{end_wait}
I nearly joined that\ncaravan. I keep thinking\nabout the men who did.{end_wait}
Hammet made Kalay what it\nis. But even if he never\ncomes home, the people{page_break}still have to eat.{end_wait}
You went into Lunpa,\n{actor_name:1}? Did you know what\ncould have happened to you?{end_wait}
Dodonpa is keeping Hammet\nalive because he can demand\nmore money. I hate that{page_break}we're forced to pay him.{end_wait}
They can take every coin I\nown. I only want Hammet\nback.{end_wait}
{actor_name:3}, there you are!\nAnd you've brought your\nfriends. We need to speak{page_break}at once.{end_wait}
Take the Shaman's Rod to\nHesperia. I wish I could\ntell you what waits there.{page_break}Be careful.{end_wait}

Kalay still doesn't know
Hammet is home. Until we're
sure Dodonpa has stopped{page_break}searching, he stays inside
the palace.{end_wait}
You brought Hammet back. I\ndon't know what else to say\nbut thank you.{end_wait}

We're keeping Hammet's
return quiet. The people
deserve to know, but we{page_break}can't risk another
kidnapping.{end_wait}
The passage below is open.\nLady Layana said you could\nenter.{end_wait}
Hammet is safe here, I\nhope. But Dodonpa has men\neverywhere. I keep checking{page_break}the doors.{end_wait}
The treasure is stored\nbeyond that passage. We\nkeep it locked when no one{page_break}is using it.{end_wait}
Layana had to speak harshly\nto {actor_name:1}. I know it hurt\nher. I hope they understand{page_break}why.{end_wait}
He's finally home.\n{actor_name:1}, {actor_name:3}, I can't\nthank you enough.{end_wait}
Hammet made it home. After\nall those weeks, it still\ndoesn't seem real.{end_wait}
I have to speak to people\nas if nothing happened.\nThey keep asking after him,{page_break}and I have to smile.{end_wait}

Layana opened the passage
as thanks to {actor_name:1} and
the others. She wanted them{page_break}to know their help
mattered.{end_wait}
We're guarding every\nentrance now. Dodonpa won't\ntake Hammet from us again.{end_wait}
One key opens both the\nhidden passage and Hammet's\ntreasure room. Best not to{page_break}lose it.{end_wait}
